result.topic_en: Derivation of the minimal-surface condition for a surface given implicitly by F, reducing it to a divergence equation and then, for a special form of F, to an ordinary differential equation in x that is integrated once.
result.transcription:
oder
$0 = \frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\right)}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}\right)}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial z}\right)}{\partial z}$
$- \frac{1}{\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}}\left[\frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\right)}{\partial x}\cdot\frac{\partial F}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}\right)}{\partial x}\frac{\partial F}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial z}\right)}{\partial x}\frac{\partial F}{\partial z}\right]$
Der Inhalt der letzten Klammer
zieht sich zusammen in
$\frac{n}{2}\frac{\partial\left(n\cdot\frac{1}{n^2}\right)}{\partial x} + \frac{1}{n^2}\cdot\frac{\partial n}{\partial x}$
d. h. in $0$, so daß die Minimal-
bedingung lautet.
$\frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\right)}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}\right)}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial\left(n\frac{\partial F}{\partial z}\right)}{\partial z} = 0.$
beachtet man bei Ausführung der
Differentiation, daß
$\frac{\partial^2 F}{[-\partial x-]\partial y^2} = 2, \quad \frac{\partial^2 F}{[-\partial x-]\partial z^2} = 2, \quad \frac{\partial^2 F}{\partial y\partial z} = 0$
ist, so erhält man
$\frac{\partial^2 F}{\partial x^2}\left[\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial z}\right)^2\right] + 2\left[\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial z}\right)^2\right] + 4\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\right)^2$
$- \frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\cdot\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial z}\right)^2\right) = 0$
oder, da $\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial z}\right)^2 = 4\left[F + \alpha^2 + \beta^2 - \gamma\right]$
ist:
$4\frac{\partial^2 F}{\partial x^2}\left(F + \alpha^2 + \beta^2 - \gamma\right) + 4\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\cdot\frac{\partial F}{\partial x} - 4\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\cdot\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(F + \alpha^2 + \beta^2 - \gamma\right)$
$+ 2.4\left(F + \alpha^2 + \beta^2 - \gamma\right) = 0$
oder
(1) $[-4-]\frac{\partial^2 F}{\partial x^2}\cdot\left(\alpha^2 + \beta^2 - \gamma\right) - \frac{\partial F}{\partial x}\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\alpha^2 + \beta^2 - \gamma\right) + 2\left(\alpha^2 + \beta^2 - \gamma\right) = 0$
Aus dieser Gleichung folgt durch
einmalige Integration, wenn man
zur Abkürzung $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 - \gamma = q$[?] setzt:
$\frac{\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}}{q} + 2\int\frac{dx}{q} + \mathrm{const.} = 0$
Die Integrationscon[...]
$x$ unabhängig. Nimm[?] [...]
seits[?] $\int\frac{dx}{q}$ unabh[...]
